title: LIGHT IN THE PLACES WHERE GOD'S PEOPLE LIVED

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "No one could see anyone else or move about for three days. Yet all the Israelites had light in the places where they lived." - Exodus 10:23 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Two sentences, side by side, describing the same three days. Egypt: no one could see anyone else or leave their home. Goshen: light in the places where they lived.

Notice what the darkness did to Egypt. It isolated people. Nobody could see anyone else. Nobody could move. That is often what darkness does — it cuts us off, convinces us we are alone, and keeps us in the house.

The Israelites had light where they lived. Not in some distant sanctuary; right in their homes, in the middle of a dark country.

We should not read this as a promise of a trouble-free life. Believers do walk through dark valleys. But it is a picture of something true: the light we have does not come from our circumstances. It comes from God, and it reaches into the ordinary rooms where we actually live.

Jesus said, I am the light of the world; whoever follows me will never walk in darkness (Jn 8:12). And He then said something remarkable to ordinary people: you are the light of the world (Mt 5:14).

If you have light, someone nearby is sitting in the dark.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where has God given me light that someone else needs?
2. Is darkness isolating me, and whom should I reach out to?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord Jesus, You are the light of the world. Shine in my home, and let Your light in me reach someone in the dark. Amen.
